items.question: A deal has stalled and the buyer is asking for 10% off. What do you do?
items.subject_said: I walk away from a stalled deal rather than discount

items.question: What does discounting to close cost you beyond the margin on that deal?
items.subject_said: Discounting to close teaches the buyer that waiting works

items.question: Demand is forecast to double next quarter. Do you hire now?
items.subject_said: I will not hire ahead of demand

items.question: You want a presence in a new city. Own the store or find a partner?
items.subject_said: I would rather find a local partner than open our own store

items.question: What is the part of a partnership you cannot verify?
items.subject_said: a partner's numbers are not mine to see

items.question: What number decides whether a store opens?
items.subject_said: below 1,200 a store never reaches breakeven

items.question: What has to be in hand before you sign for a site?
items.subject_said: I will not sign anything before I have that figure for the specific site

items.question: What do you require before agreeing to a meeting?
items.subject_said: I do not take a meeting without the previous quarter's numbers in front of me

items.question: A deal is stuck. What is the first thing you ask?
items.subject_said: how long it has been stalled

items.question: Someone brings you a plan. Where do you look first?
items.subject_said: I look for the step that has never been done before

items.question: Why own the store rather than licence the name?
items.subject_said: owning the site is the only way to hold the standard

items.question: What did you believe about ownership, before you changed your mind?
items.subject_said: I used to think ownership was the only way to hold a standard
